newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged to up slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged to up slightly.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged to up slightly as another day of new issues loomed, traders said.

Municipals continued to underperform U.S. Treasuries. Delphis Hanover Corp said Tuesday that long-term, triple-A rated municipal bonds are yielding on average 83.8 percent of the Treasury long bond, compared to 82.8 percent Monday.
Supply is still a factor in the municipal market, although not as much as Tuesday's $2.2 billion sales slate, which dulled a municipal rally.
The December municipal contract was up 7/32 to 115-8/32, while the Treasury contract was 1/32 lower at 112-18/32.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.436 billion in 39 offerings for Wednesday, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $392 million in 21 offerings, with a $132 million Virginia Public School Authority offering at 1100 EST the largest offering.
Negotiated sales total $1.144 billion in 18 offerings.
The largest issue is a $595 million New York State Urban Development Corp issue structured as senior and junior lien revenue bonds through PaineWebber Inc.
So far Wednesday morning two large issues, a $90 million Mercy Health System and a $100 million Connecticut revenue bond offering have been priced.

Bear Stearns & Co tentatively priced $90 million of Mercy Health System hospital revenue and refunding bonds, Series 1996 B. The bonds have insurance from AMBAC Indemnity Corp and MBIA Insurance Corp.
Goldman Sachs & Co tentatively priced $100 million Connecticut revenue bonds at a top yield of 5.55 percent in 2012.
In secondary market activity, Denver Airport 5.50s due in 2025 were bid 5.77 percent, down five basis points from 5.82 percent on Tuesday.
